concepts.name: Managed Delivery
concepts.text: No shards to provision; auto-scales and buffers by size or time before delivering to S3, Redshift, OpenSearch, Iceberg, Splunk or HTTP.

concepts.name: Lambda Transform
concepts.text: Invokes Lambda on record batches to enrich, filter, mask or reformat (e.g. CSV to JSON); returns Ok, Dropped or ProcessingFailed.

concepts.name: Format Conversion
concepts.text: Converts JSON input to Parquet or ORC in flight using a Glue Data Catalog table schema; non-JSON must be converted by Lambda first.

concepts.name: Dynamic Partitions
concepts.text: Builds S3 prefixes from record fields via inline JQ or Lambda, creating query-friendly partitions without a separate ETL job.

items.label: Ingest & Buffer
items.text: Receive from Direct PUT, Kinesis Data Streams or MSK; buffer records until size or time hint is reached.

items.label: Transform/Convert
items.text: Optionally run Lambda transforms, convert JSON to Parquet/ORC via Glue schema, and extract partition keys.

items.label: Deliver & Backup
items.text: Deliver batches (Redshift stages via S3 + COPY); route failed records or raw copies to S3 backup prefixes.

table.heading: Firehose Capabilities
rows: Buffering
Batches by size or time hint before delivery
Near real time; larger buffers avoid small S3 files
Format conversion
Converts JSON to Parquet or ORC in flight
Needs Glue Data Catalog schema; CSV needs Lambda first
Dynamic partitioning
Extracts S3 prefix keys via inline JQ or Lambda
Produces Hive-style S3 partitions without ETL jobs
Error & raw backup
Writes failed records or raw copies to S3 prefix
Redshift retries COPY, then writes failed manifest to S3
Replay & consumers
Single delivery pipe; no log retention
Pair with Kinesis Data Streams for replay or multi-consumer

tips: Firehose is near real time (seconds to minutes) due to buffering; 'milliseconds' points to Kinesis Data Streams.
Format conversion requires JSON input and a Glue Data Catalog table schema; convert CSV to JSON with Lambda first.
No replay and no multiple consumers: put Kinesis Data Streams in front of Firehose when you need either.
Small buffers create many small S3 files that hurt Athena; Redshift delivery always stages through S3 and runs COPY.
